arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The government argued Congress must clearly waive sovereign immunity for emotional distress.
The employee argued the statute protects against recognized common law harms.
Justice Ginsburg questioned whether emotional distress qualifies as an actual injury.
Justice Sotomayor asked why emotional distress differs from actual injury.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of the Privacy Act. It asks if the statute waives sovereign immunity for non-pecuniary harms. The lower court allowed the claim to proceed. The government seeks to limit damages to pecuniary losses.

paragraphs: This case defines the scope of federal liability for privacy violations. It determines whether citizens can recover for non-pecuniary harms. The outcome shapes the balance between government accountability and sovereign immunity.
